title: Mild third-trimester thrombocytopenia: gestational thrombocytopenia (hemodilution + placental sequestration)
vignette: A 24-year-old woman, gravida 1 para 0, at 28 weeks gestation comes to the office for a routine prenatal visit. She feels well and has had no vaginal bleeding, contractions, or leakage of fluid. Fetal movement is normal. The patient has no chronic medical conditions and her pregnancy has been uncomplicated. She previously had heavy menstrual periods that were managed with oral contraceptives. Blood pressure is 126/84 mm Hg and pulse is 78/min. Fundal height and fetal heart tones are normal. Today's third-trimester complete blood count shows hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, platelets 120,000/mm3, and leukocytes 8,200/mm3. Coagulation studies and peripheral smear are within normal limits. The patient's first-trimester platelet count was 160,000/mm3. Urine dipstick today is negative for protein. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's thrombocytopenia?

clues.note: Mild thrombocytopenia (120,000 / normal 150,000-400,000) that is asymptomatic in the third trimester is typical of gestational thrombocytopenia.
A gradual, mild fall from a normal first-trimester count fits the dilutional/physiologic drop of pregnancy (gestational thrombocytopenia), not an acute pathologic process.
No proteinuria (and normal BP) argues against preeclampsia/HELLP as the cause of thrombocytopenia.

whatMatters: Mild, asymptomatic third-trimester thrombocytopenia with a normal smear/coagulation, no proteinuria, and no other abnormalities = GESTATIONAL THROMBOCYTOPENIA. It arises from HEMODILUTION (plasma volume expansion) and INCREASED PLATELET SEQUESTRATION/consumption in the placenta. Answer C.
strategy: Recognize gestational thrombocytopenia: mild (usually >=100,000), late-pregnancy, asymptomatic, normal smear/coagulation, no other cause - benign and self-limited. Mechanism = hemodilution + placental sequestration. Reject DIC (bleeding, abnormal coagulation studies), decreased thromboxane A2 (aspirin effect - not thrombocytopenia), immune complex/complement activation (autoimmune, e.g., SLE), and platelet microthrombi (TTP/HELLP - microangiopathy with abnormal smear/organ injury).

options.text: Small vessel formation of platelet microthrombi

eliminations.label: Coagulation-activated thrombi - DIC
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: widespread coagulation activation consuming platelets (DIC). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: DIC causes bleeding and ABNORMAL coagulation studies; this patient's coagulation studies and smear are normal and she is asymptomatic. ✅ Correct if: bleeding with prolonged PT/PTT, low fibrinogen, high D-dimer.

eliminations.label: Decreased thromboxane A2 - aspirin effect
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: reduced thromboxane A2 (aspirin) impairing platelet aggregation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this affects platelet FUNCTION, not count; aspirin users typically have normal/elevated platelet counts. ✅ Correct if: bleeding tendency with normal platelet count (aspirin).

eliminations.label: Immune complex/complement - autoimmune
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: immune-complex-mediated complement activation (e.g., SLE). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: no autoimmune features are present, and gestational thrombocytopenia is not immune-complex mediated (it is dilutional/sequestration). ✅ Correct if: SLE or other immune-complex disease with other symptoms.

eliminations.label: Platelet microthrombi - TTP/HELLP microangiopathy
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: microvascular platelet thrombi (TTP/HELLP). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: those cause microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (schistocytes on smear) and end-organ injury; here the smear is normal and there's no hemolysis/proteinuria. ✅ Correct if: MAHA + thrombocytopenia +/- neuro/renal or HELLP (with hypertension/proteinuria).

reasoning: Mild, asymptomatic thrombocytopenia (120,000) in the third trimester with normal smear/coagulation
No proteinuria or hypertension (argues against preeclampsia/HELLP) and no other cause
This is gestational thrombocytopenia, from hemodilution and increased placental sequestration/consumption
-> hemodilution and increased platelet sequestration; answer C
mechanism: GESTATIONAL THROMBOCYTOPENIA (GT) is a benign, self-limited condition and the most common cause of thrombocytopenia in pregnancy, typically diagnosed in the THIRD TRIMESTER when it is often an incidental finding. Two physiologic processes drive it: (1) PLASMA VOLUME EXPANSION - maternal plasma volume increases ~30-50% during pregnancy (to support fetal delivery and buffer delivery blood loss), producing HEMODILUTION that lowers the platelet CONCENTRATION even though platelet production is unchanged; and (2) increased platelet SEQUESTRATION/CONSUMPTION in the highly vascular PLACENTA (platelets pool and are consumed in the intervillous space). GT is characteristically MILD (platelets usually >=100,000), ASYMPTOMATIC (no bleeding/bruising), with NORMAL coagulation studies and a NORMAL peripheral smear, and it resolves after delivery. It is distinguished from DIC (bleeding, abnormal coagulation), immune thrombocytopenia (lower counts), and the pregnancy-specific microangiopathies preeclampsia/HELLP and TTP (hypertension/proteinuria, hemolysis with schistocytes, organ injury) - none of which fit this normotensive, protein-negative, smear-normal patient.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid OB/Physiology > gestational thrombocytopenia: most common pregnancy thrombocytopenia; mild (>=100,000), third trimester, asymptomatic, normal smear/coagulation; hemodilution (plasma volume expansion) + placental sequestration; resolves postpartum; distinguish from HELLP/preeclampsia/ITP/TTP.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Mild asymptomatic third-trimester thrombocytopenia, normal smear, no proteinuria = gestational (dilution + sequestration).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on gestational thrombocytopenia, plasma volume expansion/hemodilution, placental sequestration, or HELLP/preeclampsia? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: DIC = abnormal coagulation/bleeding; thromboxane = platelet function (aspirin); immune complex = autoimmune; microthrombi = TTP/HELLP (abnormal smear).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: gestational thrombocytopenia = mild, third-trimester, benign; hemodilution + placental platelet sequestration; normal smear/coags.

keywords.back: Mild (>=100,000), 3rd trimester, asymptomatic, normal smear/coags; resolves postpartum

firstAid.detail: OB: hemodilution + placental sequestration; mild, benign, 3rd trimester.
OB > DIC, HELLP/preeclampsia, ITP, TTP differ.

memoryHook: More plasma (dilution) plus a hungry placenta soaking up platelets = a mild late-pregnancy platelet dip that's harmless: gestational thrombocytopenia.
